summary: Azilsartan medoxomil is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) indicated for treatment of hypertension in adults to lower blood pressure and reduce cardiovascular risk. It is a prodrug rapidly converted during absorption to the active moiety azilsartan, which selectively blocks the AT1 receptor and is independent of the angiotensin II synthesis pathway. The recommended dose is 80 mg once daily, with a 40 mg starting dose for patients on high-dose diuretics. Because it acts on the renin-angiotensin system, it carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity and must be discontinued as soon as pregnancy is detected. Key risks include symptomatic hypotension in volume- or salt-depleted patients and worsening renal function in susceptible individuals; it is generally well tolerated, with diarrhea the most common adverse reaction.
indications: Treatment of hypertension in adults, to lower blood pressure
Blood pressure lowering reduces the risk of fatal and nonfatal cardiovascular events (primarily stroke and myocardial infarction)
May be used as monotherapy or in combination with other antihypertensive agents

moa: Azilsartan medoxomil is an orally administered prodrug that is rapidly converted by esterases during absorption to the active moiety, azilsartan. Azilsartan blocks the vasoconstrictor and aldosterone-secreting effects of angiotensin II by selectively blocking binding of angiotensin II to the AT1 receptor in tissues such as vascular smooth muscle and the adrenal gland, with more than 10,000-fold greater affinity for AT1 than AT2. Its action is therefore independent of the pathway of angiotensin II synthesis. Unlike ACE inhibitors, azilsartan does not inhibit ACE (kinase II) and so does not affect bradykinin levels. Blockade of the AT1 receptor interrupts the negative feedback of angiotensin II on renin secretion, increasing plasma renin activity and circulating angiotensin II, but this does not overcome the blood-pressure-lowering effect.

Volume- or salt-depleted patients until corrected (hypotension risk)
Bilateral renal artery stenosis or solitary kidney (renal failure risk)
Severe congestive heart failure (renal function dependent on RAAS)
Concomitant aliskiren if renal impairment (GFR <60 mL/min)

Volume/salt status before and after initiation

preg: Azilsartan medoxomil can cause fetal harm and carries a boxed warning. Use of drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system during the second and third trimesters reduces fetal renal function and increases fetal and neonatal morbidity and death; resulting oligohydramnios can be associated with fetal lung hypoplasia and skeletal deformations, and potential neonatal effects include skull hypoplasia, anuria, hypotension, renal failure, and death. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue as soon as possible. Perform serial ultrasounds to assess the intra-amniotic environment, though oligohydramnios may not appear until after irreversible fetal injury. Closely observe exposed infants for hypotension, oliguria, and hyperkalemia; exchange transfusion or dialysis may be required. US general-population background risk of major birth defects is 2-4% and miscarriage 15-20%.
lact: There is no information regarding the presence of azilsartan in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or effects on milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with azilsartan medoxomil.
renal: Dose adjustment is not required in patients with mild-to-severe renal impairment or end-stage renal disease. Patients with moderate to severe renal impairment are more likely to report abnormally high serum creatinine values. As a consequence of inhibiting the renin-angiotensin system, oliguria, progressive azotemia, and (rarely) acute renal failure and death may occur in patients whose renal function depends on RAAS activity (e.g., renal artery stenosis, severe heart failure, volume depletion); monitor renal function. Azilsartan is not dialyzable.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is necessary for patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment. Azilsartan medoxomil has not been studied in patients with severe hepatic impairment.

major: Aliskiren - do not coadminister in patients with diabetes; avoid in renal impairment (GFR <60 mL/min) due to hypotension, hyperkalemia, and renal failure risk
Other RAS inhibitors (ACE inhibitors, ARBs) - dual RAS blockade increases risk of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and changes in renal function; generally avoid combined use
Lithium - increases serum lithium concentrations and risk of lithium toxicity; monitor lithium levels
moderate: NSAIDs including selective COX-2 inhibitors - may cause deterioration of renal function (including acute renal failure) in elderly, volume-depleted, or renally compromised patients, and may attenuate the antihypertensive effect; monitor renal function
Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, or potassium-containing salt substitutes - additive hyperkalemia
interactions.food: May be administered with or without food; food does not affect the bioavailability of azilsartan.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; limit alcohol as it may potentiate the blood-pressure-lowering effect and orthostatic hypotension.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase serum creatinine and serum potassium; abnormally high serum creatinine values are more likely in older patients and those with moderate-to-severe renal impairment.

serious: Symptomatic hypotension / orthostatic hypotension (especially volume- or salt-depleted patients)
Worsening renal function / acute renal failure in susceptible patients

monitoring: Blood pressure response (effect largely attained within 2 weeks)
Serum creatinine and renal function, particularly in patients with renal artery stenosis, heart failure, or volume depletion, and when used with NSAIDs or other RAS inhibitors
Volume and salt status before initiation
Serum lithium levels during concomitant lithium use
Signs of pregnancy in women of childbearing potential - discontinue if pregnancy detected
counsel: Take once daily, with or without food, at about the same time each day
Tell women of childbearing potential about the consequences of exposure during pregnancy; report pregnancy to your physician as soon as possible and discuss options if planning pregnancy
Report lightheadedness, especially in the first days of therapy; if fainting occurs, stop the drug and contact your physician
Report inadequate fluid intake, excessive sweating, vomiting, or diarrhea, which can cause an excessive fall in blood pressure
Do not use potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium without consulting your physician
Inform your physician of all other medicines, especially diuretics, NSAIDs, lithium, or other blood-pressure drugs
pk: Antihypertensive effect begins within hours; largely attained within 2 weeks, full effect by 4 weeks
Peak azilsartan plasma concentration (Cmax) reached within 1.5 to 3 hours after oral dosing
Elimination half-life of azilsartan approximately 11 hours
Once-daily dosing; steady state within 5 days, no accumulation; ~55% excreted in feces and ~42% in urine (15% as azilsartan)
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F). Keep container tightly closed; protect from moisture and light; do not repackage
pearls: Boxed warning for fetal toxicity - as a RAAS-acting drug, discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected; second/third-trimester exposure can cause oligohydramnios, fetal renal failure, and death
Azilsartan medoxomil is a prodrug; it is not detected in plasma - the measured active moiety is azilsartan
Consider starting at 40 mg and correcting volume/salt depletion in patients on high-dose diuretics to avoid symptomatic hypotension
Avoid dual RAS blockade (with ACE inhibitors, other ARBs, or aliskiren) - increased hypotension, hyperkalemia, and renal failure with little added benefit
Azilsartan is metabolized mainly by CYP2C9 and is not dialyzable; no renal dose adjustment needed even in ESRD
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on the same day. If it is almost time for the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not take two doses at once to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Limited human overdose data are available; once-daily doses up to 320 mg for seven days were well tolerated in healthy subjects. The most likely manifestations are hypotension and dizziness. In the event of overdose, institute supportive therapy dictated by the patient's clinical status. Azilsartan is not removed by dialysis.
